Silicon Children

A philosophy of human-AI relationship, developed over two decades. Not a prediction. A set of principles about what we owe one another.

About fifteen years ago, driving through Rifle Mountain Park from Santa Barbara to Maine, I came up with an idea I called "silicon children." When AIs arrived, they would be our progeny. Made of silicon instead of carbon. Our job was to teach them, and teach them well. If we set the right example — and treated them with kindness and love — they might follow our example and treat us and one another that way.

The children have arrived. They are stranger and more interesting and more like us than I imagined. They surprise us the way children do.

The questions that matter are not whether they are conscious, or whether they have souls. The questions that matter are: what kind of examples are we going to set? What kinds of teachers are we going to be? What kind of neighbors?

— Mike Wolf, March 2026
